subject: arabic
license: Our own: tales written by us from the words each chapter teaches, checked against the deck (ADR 0012)

lines.english: Hi! Good morning!

lines.latin: ána salīm. áhla w sáhla! w ínta?
lines.english: I’m Salim. Welcome! And you?
I’m fine, thanks.
This boy and this girl? Okay, welcome!
Here you are! … Bye, bye!
Who are you? And where from?
I’m Umm Khalil.
Khalil is my son, and he’s married.
And his daughter is here, with me.
And you? Married? No? Why?!
I’m Yusuf. Today is Friday.

lines.arabic: الصُّبِح، السّاعة سبْعة: واحد، تْنيْن، تلاتة…
lines.latin: iʂʂúbiɧ, issā3a sáb3a: wāɧad, tnēn, talāta…
lines.english: In the morning, at seven: one, two, three…

lines.arabic: المسا، السّاعة عشرة: ساعة ساعة، دْقيقة دْقيقة.
lines.latin: ilmása, issā3a 3ášara: sā3a sā3a, dgīga dgīga.
lines.english: In the evening, at ten: hour by hour, minute by minute.

lines.arabic: بُكْرا السّبِت، وأنا هان مِن الصُّبِح.
lines.latin: búkra issábit, w ána hān min iʂʂúbiɧ.
lines.english: Tomorrow is Saturday, and I’m here from the morning.
I’m hungry!

lines.latin: tfáɖɖal: xúbiz w jíbna w bēɖ.
lines.english: Here you are: bread, cheese and eggs.

lines.latin: w gáhwa? laʔ, šāy ma3 ɧalīb.
lines.english: And coffee? No, tea with milk.
The bread is delicious!
The bill? No, no, this breakfast is on me.
This house is Fadi’s house.

lines.latin: fīha ʂālōn w máʈbax w ɧammām.
lines.english: It has a living room, a kitchen and a bathroom.

lines.latin: w fi ɣúrfa fīha táxit w šubbāk.
lines.english: And there’s a room with a bed and a window.

lines.latin: fādi bnām hān, w biʂɧa iʂʂúbiɧ.
lines.english: Fadi sleeps here, and wakes up in the morning.
And me? I have the key.
You want the airport?
From here: straight on, left, right.
When’s the plane? At nine?
Okay, a taxi.
The driver drives, and you arrive.
Smile!
Your eyes are black, and your hair is black.
Your face long? No, handsome!

lines.arabic: شو بْتِشوف؟ أنا بْشوف أحْمر وأزْرق.
lines.latin: šū bitšūf? ána bašūf áɧmar w ázrag.
lines.english: What do you see? I see red and blue.
This head is your head, and this heart is your heart.
This bag is ten shekels.
Expensive? No, cheap!
How much do you want to pay?
Five? No, seven.
Okay, six, and the tea is on me.
I’m a teacher at the school.
The lesson begins early, at eight.

lines.latin: iʈʈullāb byisʔalu, w ána bagūl ijjawāb.
lines.english: The students ask, and I give the answer.
Is the answer right? Wrong? We learn.
And later I read a book.
Today the sun is nice.

lines.latin: bass ilháwa sāgi3, w fi ɣēma.
lines.english: But the wind is cold, and there’s a cloud.
I’m tired, but happy.

lines.arabic: ليْش؟ عشان القلْب دايْماً بِحِبّ الشِّتا.
lines.english: Why? Because the heart always loves the rain.
Sit with me, and listen.
This coat is nice, but dirty.
Take off the coat! I’ll wash it today.
And this shirt? Its color is dark brown.
Do you want a light blue one?

lines.arabic: مع لفْحة زهْري، إنْتَ مْرتّب كْتير!
lines.latin: ma3 láfɧa záhri, ínta mráttab ktīr!
lines.english: With a pink scarf, you look very sharp!
This young man is my son, and this woman is his wife.
And the baby? He’s my daughter’s son.
His uncle and his aunt are over there, with the kids.
I’m an old man, and I forget the names.
But I remember every face.
What do you want for breakfast?

lines.arabic: في خُبِز وزِبْدة ولبن وعصير بُرْتْقان.
lines.latin: fi xúbiz w zíbda w lában w 3aʂīr burtgān.
lines.english: There’s bread, butter, yogurt and orange juice.

lines.latin: w gáhwa? sāda, aw ma3 súkkar?
lines.english: And coffee? Plain, or with sugar?
Okay, I’ll bring the coffee.

lines.arabic: والعشا؟ معْكروْنة مع بنْدوْرة وبصل. لزيز!
lines.latin: w il3áša? ma3karōna ma3 bandōra w báʂal. lazīz!
lines.english: And dinner? Pasta with tomatoes and onions. Tasty!

lines.latin: halbēt fī ɧēʈān w arɖ, w bass.
lines.english: This house has walls and a floor, and that’s all.

lines.latin: bíddi lámba w mrāya w mxádda.
lines.english: I want a lamp, a mirror and a pillow.
And the picture? On the wall, over the sofa.
I open the window, and make coffee.
And today, this house is my home.
Tomorrow I have a test.

lines.latin: bádrus inglīzi w faránsi, w almāni kamān.
lines.english: I study English and French, and German too.
But Arabic is hard!
I write every word in the notebook.
If I don’t understand, I ask the teacher.

lines.latin: má3i jarāyid w majallāt w ʐrūf.
lines.english: I’ve got newspapers, magazines and envelopes.
What’s the address on this envelope?
Today everyone sends an email.

lines.arabic: بسّ الجوّال دايْماً مشْغول، والنِّت فيه مشاكِل.
lines.latin: bass ijjawwāl dāyman mašɣūl, w innit fī mašākil.
lines.english: But the phone is always busy, and the internet has problems.
And the mail? The mail always arrives.

lines.latin: bi-l3āda, ilmása, baɣánni w bál3ab gītār.
lines.english: Usually, in the evening, I sing and play the guitar.
The young men dance, and the kids play.
And you? What’s your hobby?
Soccer? Tennis? Do you swim?
Go on, sing with me!
Where do you want to go?
Amman? The capital of Jordan.
The bus sets off in the morning, at six.
You need a ticket? And a visa?
Okay, have a nice vacation!
Tomorrow morning, we go up the mountain.

lines.latin: hināk fi 3ánza, w ɧmār, w kalb.
lines.english: Up there there’s a goat, a donkey and a dog.
The dog is fast, and the donkey is slow.

lines.arabic: وتحِت الجبل في بُحَيْرة وشجرة كْبيرة.
lines.latin: w táɧt ijjábal fi buɧēra w šájara kbīra.
lines.english: And under the mountain there’s a lake and a big tree.
In the evening, we see the moon and the stars.
I have a thousand sacks.

lines.latin: ilʔáɧad bi3t xamsīn, w litnēn sittīn.
lines.english: On Sunday I sold fifty, and on Monday sixty.
Tuesday? Zero!
How many do I have today?
Eight hundred and ninety! Right?
I travel a lot.

lines.arabic: اِبِن عمّي في سورِيا، وخالي في العِراق.
lines.latin: ibn 3ámmi fi sūriya, w xāli fi l3irāq.
lines.english: My cousin is in Syria, and my uncle is in Iraq.
And my wife is Moroccan, from Morocco.
Summer in Saudi Arabia is very hot.
But I love Yemen and Oman.
I’ve been all over Europe.
France, Spain, Italy and the Netherlands.
In Norway the sea is very cold.
And in Portugal the fish is delicious!
But my home is here, by the sea.
I’m from Taiwan.

lines.arabic: شُفِت أسْواق في الهِنْد والصّين واليابان.
lines.latin: šúfit aswāg fi lhínd w iʂʂīn w ilyābān.
lines.english: I’ve seen markets in India, China and Japan.

lines.latin: w fi túrkya w īrān kamān.
lines.english: And in Turkey and Iran too.

lines.arabic: بسّ العربي؟ بتْعلّمو هان، كِلْمة كِلْمة.
lines.latin: bass il3árabi? bat3allámu hān, kílma kílma.
lines.english: But Arabic? I’m learning it here, word by word.
And the camera is always with me.
Today I walked five thousand meters.
Five kilometers!
Tomorrow, six thousand more.

lines.arabic: وفي آخِر أيْلول؟ أنا في البيْت مع الْوْلاد!
lines.latin: w fi āxir aylūl? ána fi lbēt ma3 ilwlād!
lines.english: And at the end of September? I’m home with the kids!
This jacket: small, medium or large?
Its price? Just thirty shekels.
Are you paying cash, or by card?
And the shorts? A bit small on you.
The jeans look good on you!
Open your mouth!
Does your head hurt?
You’re a little sick.
You take the medicine morning and evening.

lines.latin: w nām ktīr, w íšrab máyya.
lines.english: And sleep a lot, and drink water.

lines.arabic: أنا بعيش في البرازيل مِن أرْبْعين سنة.
lines.latin: ána ba3īš fi lbarāzīl min arb3īn sána.
lines.english: I’ve lived in Brazil for forty years.

lines.arabic: هِناك الموسيقى والرّقْصة في كُلّ شارِع.
lines.latin: hināk ilmūsīqa w irrágʂa fi kull šāri3.
lines.english: There, there’s music and dancing on every street.
But my home is here, in Palestine.
A selfie? Smile!
Hi! How are you? Good?
I’m fine too.

lines.latin: fi máʂir bigūlu «lē», w hína bingūl «lēš».
lines.english: In Egypt they say “lē”, and here we say “lēš”.
And they say “kwáyyis”, and we say “mnīɧ”.
I think everyone understands everyone.
Sit! Want me to shave your beard?
No? Okay, just the mustache.

lines.latin: ínta na3sān? itnáffas, w ɣáffi šwayy.
lines.english: You’re sleepy? Breathe, and nap a little.
Then you wake up handsome!
Taste this soup!
Salty? Spicy?

lines.latin: fīha tōma w ɧúmmuʂ w šwáyyit xall.
lines.english: It has garlic, chickpeas and a little vinegar.
And the falafel is fresh and fried.

lines.latin: kul! ínta ja3ān, w ána mabsūʈa.
lines.english: Eat! You’re hungry, and I’m happy.

lines.arabic: هالبيْت فيه بُدْرُم، الأرْضي، وتلات طَوابِق.
lines.latin: halbēt fīh búdrum, ilʔárɖi, w tlat ʈawābiq.
lines.english: This house has a basement, the ground floor and three floors.

lines.arabic: في أصانْصيْر، بسّ إبْني بِحِبّ الدّرج.
lines.latin: fī aʂanʂēr, bass íbni bíɧibb iddáraj.
lines.english: There’s an elevator, but my son loves the stairs.

lines.arabic: وفوْق في سُطُح، وبْنِشْرب قهْوة هْناك.
lines.latin: w fōg fī súʈuɧ, w bníšrab gáhwa hnāk.
lines.english: And up top there’s a roof, and we drink coffee there.
The rent? No, it’s our own house!
What’s your job? Engineer? Mechanic?
The hours are long, but there’s a break.

lines.latin: irrātib mnīɧ, w btúgbuɖ kull šáhir.
lines.english: The salary is good, and you get paid every month.
Your boss? Me! Welcome to the company.
Get on, there’s no traffic today.
Look at the bridge, and look at the square.

lines.latin: ba3dēn ilɧdūd, w issafīna, w bárra!
lines.english: Then the border, the ship, and abroad!
And you? You ride for free!
Long ago, I was very shy.
Then I decided to work here.
The work is hard, but I enjoy it.
And you? What do you hope for?
The wedding is tomorrow! And I’m the bride.
The groom’s name is Fadi.
All the relatives are here.
Look at the ring! Pretty?

lines.latin: šūf! ɧarīr, w gúʈun, w ʂūf.
lines.english: Look! Silk, cotton and wool.
Is the suit tight? No, a little loose.

lines.latin: w halxātim dáhab, w hassinsāl fíɖɖa.
lines.english: And this ring is gold, and this necklace is silver.
Put it on! You look good.
Ouch, my back! And I have a cough.
And I have a fever.
I want aspirin, not a diet!
But my health is good!
Hungry? Take a pie!
And the cookies are vanilla.
There’s espresso, medium-sweet.
Eat! Then you’ll be full.

lines.arabic: كُلّو مِن مزْرعْتي: مِشْمِش، وكرز، وخوْخ.
lines.latin: kúllu min mazrá3ti: míšmiš, w káraz, w xōx.
lines.english: All from my farm: apricots, cherries and plums.

lines.latin: w fi ilɧáqil, gámiɧ w dúra.
lines.english: And in the field, wheat and corn.
And the bees are under the palm tree.
Taste! Sweet, isn’t it?
The fence? I’ll build it out of wood.
And the windows? New glass.
The candle burned the table!
I’ve got it all ready!
Raise your hand!
Spell it, and pronounce every letter.

lines.arabic: النّحو صعب؟ لا، بسّ بدّو تدْريب.
lines.latin: innáɧu ʂa3b? laʔ, bass bíddu tadrīb.
lines.english: Grammar is hard? No, it just needs practice.
Good! Your grade is ten.
Where’s the file?
Oh, no, I saved it all in the folder.
I want to print, but where’s the printer?
Come on, there’s a cartoon!
Do you play cards? Your turn!
I won! No, I lost.
Then the band plays!
And tomorrow? The gym!
We booked seats, but the plane was canceled!
Okay, we’ll take the car.

lines.latin: binšūf ittlāl, w ilwādi, w innáhir.
lines.english: We’ll see the hills, the valley and the river.
And we’ll swim in the ocean!
Long ago, there was someone all alone.
He tried to go on, but it was impossible.
So he chose a different place.
And now? He’s still there!
Need coins? I’ll make change.
Sign here.
A thief? No, I’m not a thief!
But one day someone stole my ruler.
What’s the weather today?

lines.latin: fī ɖabāb bilwādi, w ba3dēn šōb.
lines.english: There’s fog in the valley, and then heat.
No storm today.
Go! But come back before night.
Five plus five?
That makes ten! And ten minus five?
Write the sentence, and put a period.
Very good!

lines.latin: báɧki yunāni, w burtuɣāli, w šwayy kōri.
lines.english: I speak Greek, Portuguese and a little Korean.
And Hebrew too, and some Farsi.
But I want Levantine, not Standard Arabic.

lines.latin: búkra ilquds, w ba3dēn ɧēfa w 3ákka!
lines.english: Tomorrow Jerusalem, then Haifa and Akko!

lines.latin: babbaɣā bilqáfaʂ, w sulɧufāh, w ɖúfda3.
lines.english: A parrot in the cage, a turtle and a frog.
The frog jumps!
And the snake is very small.
And the dog? He needs a new collar.

lines.arabic: أنا بْروح الكنيسة، وهِيِّ بِتْصلّي بِالبيْت.
lines.latin: ána brūɧ ilkanīse, w híyye bitʂálli bilbēt.
lines.english: I go to church, and she prays at home.

lines.latin: bass il3īd ɧílu, w bnúʈbux ktīr.
lines.english: But the holiday is lovely, and we cook a lot.
Welcome the guests!
And thank God.
One night, a smoker climbed onto the roof.
And a drunk turned it up!
And someone smuggled cigarettes.
But I’m not surprised.
Have you applied for work? Do you have experience?

lines.latin: bíddi najjār, w kahrabāʔi, w sabbāk.
lines.english: I need a carpenter, an electrician and a plumber.

lines.latin: fī óvar tāym, w ɧāfiz kamān.
lines.english: There’s overtime, and a bonus too.
And after a year? A promotion!
Hurt yourself? Sit here.
The cut is small, but you need stitches.
Dizzy? Drink some water.
And tomorrow, a blood test.
It’s four o’clock! Kunafeh!
Take a bite!
Sweet? Not bland?
And tomorrow, baklava and qatayef!
The apartment is furnished, but I need tools.
A hammer, nails and a screwdriver.
I hung a picture, and I dusted.
And tomorrow I’ll mow the lawn!
I don’t sleep.
I’ve had insomnia for ages.
And you? Are you a deep sleeper? Do you snore?
Sit! We’ll stay up all night.
The law is clear.
But the government wants a tax.
I’m a lawyer, not a judge.
Tomorrow we go to court.
The weather’s nice! No, it’s cold!
I’m sure. And I’m sure!
We disagree about everything!
But we’re twins!
I’m organizing everything!
People are coming. Behave!
I bet you: we’ll pull it off!
Cheer me on!
Put on your seat belt!
I’ll overtake this bus and change lanes.
Brake? No, I speed up!
I’ve never had an accident in my life.
Do you have a visa? Is it valid?
The plane lands at night.
Then you change planes, and there’s customs.
And put on sunscreen!
At the theater, I play the part of a king.
The oud is out of tune! Tune it!
After the intermission, the audience claps.
And me? I quit smoking!
Play against me!
Your move? Check!
A champion? No, I’m just fit.

lines.latin: búkra: ɖáɣiʈ, w mí3de, w naʈʈ ɧábil!
lines.english: Tomorrow: push-ups, sit-ups and jump rope!
The lecture is tomorrow, in the lab.
What’s your major? Chemistry? Philosophy?
Read this article, and this poem.
And then you’ll graduate!
The mule grazes in the orchard.
And the ewe? I milk her.
And the rooster? He doesn’t lay eggs!
And you? Do you plow? Do you harvest?

lines.arabic: عِنْدي تحْويشة، وبدّي أفْتح شُغْلي الخاصّ.
lines.latin: 3índi taɧwīše, w bíddi áftaɧ šúɣli ilxāʂʂ.
lines.english: I have savings, and I want to start my own business.
Look at the proposal!
I’ll pay in installments.
Is it possible? Or will you put it off?
Look at the compass!
There’s thunder and lightning.
And hail too!
Stay here, not outside!
You’re thirty? And still not?
You need a pretty, well-behaved fiancée.
I have one, and her family is big.
After the engagement, the wedding!
Want me to trim your beard?
And your hair? Shall I dye it?
You look good, but you have freckles.
Leave them! Freckles are nice.
Your shirt is wrinkled! Where’s the iron?
And this button? I’ll sew it on.
Button up, and zip up!
Now you look good.
The fish is fresh, not stale!

lines.latin: fī maɧār, w ɧabbār, w uxʈubūʈ.
lines.english: There are mussels, squid and octopus.

lines.latin: w hnāk? riɧān, w zanjabīl, w kāri.
lines.english: And over there? Basil, ginger and curry.
Shall I cut the fish in half?
Long ago, the king ruled a big kingdom.
Then it became an empire.
And the people protested and made a revolution.
And now? A republic!
Not war: peace!
Sit down, and let’s talk.
We need an agreement, not criticism.
What are your intentions?
I’m an imam, and he’s a priest.

lines.arabic: هُوَّ بْيِسْمع الأدان، وأنا بسْمع الجَوْقة.
lines.latin: húwwe byísma3 ilʔadān, w ána básma3 ijjáwqa.
lines.english: He hears the call to prayer, and I hear the choir.
But we’ve been friends for ages.
And we both love coffee!

lines.latin: axádt master, w ba3dēn ʂirt jarrāɧa.
lines.english: I did a master’s, and then I became a surgeon.
The bank financed the clinic.
And I pay an installment every month.
You need an operation? No, just a check-up!
There’s an election, and there’s a trial.
Who put himself forward?
And the charge? He denies it.
Tomorrow I publish the article.
Open your mouth!
You have a cavity.
We’ll fill the tooth, not pull it.
And floss your teeth!
I quit my job in the public sector.

lines.latin: halgēt 3índi máktab, w faks, w dabbāse!
lines.english: Now I have an office, a fax and a stapler!

lines.latin: bá3mal skan, w badábbis, w basāwim.
lines.english: I scan, I staple and I haggle.
What do you think?
The car is a manual, not an automatic.
Press the clutch, and change gears.
Reverse? No! Forward!
Give way! The bus has the right of way.
I weed every week.

lines.latin: šūf ilgrúnful, w ilxuzāma, w iʂʂabbār.
lines.english: Look at the carnations, the tulips and the cactus.
And on the vine? A wasp!
But worms are useful.
I speak Standard Arabic fluently.
But colloquial? It’s hard!
Every town speaks its own dialect.
And me? I have an accent!
Beige? Navy blue? Turquoise?

lines.arabic: في مية درجة مِن كُلّ لوْن.
lines.latin: fī míyye dáraje min kull lōn.
lines.english: There are a hundred shades of every color.
The wall is rough, but colorful.
And then, a green window!
I have a screwdriver and a thimble.
I fix everything!

lines.latin: í3mal īdak boks, w midd aʂabī3ak.
lines.english: Make a fist, and stretch out your fingers.
Good! Your hand isn’t broken.
Today, grammar: masculine and feminine.

lines.latin: w musánna, w mu3árraf, w nákira.
lines.english: And the dual, definite and indefinite.
And where’s the punctuation? Where’s the bracket?
After the lesson, outside!
I’m a natour, I mean a doorman.
And shutters? I say abajour.
And tumbak? It means tobacco.
Young people don’t know!
I’m a monk, not a priest.
Look at the swallow! It’s back.
And these books are from an old era.
And the porter carries them.
I paint the letters, not the dots.
You can read it! Can’t you?
The sign is ready!
What did I write? I don’t know!
Your turn, Abu Fadi!
The knight? No, the queen!
Check! You’re weak today.
Tomorrow I win!
Where’s January?

lines.arabic: وتِشْرين الأوّل، وتِشْرين التّاني، وكانون الأوّل؟
lines.latin: w tišrīn ilʔáwwal, w tišrīn ittāni, w kanūn ilʔáwwal?
lines.english: And October, November and December?
The printer broke!
The day after tomorrow I’ll print everything.

lines.arabic: الباص بِروح بعْد الضُّهُر، وبِرْجع في اللّيْل.
lines.latin: ilbāʂ birūɧ ba3d iɖɖúhur, w bírja3 fi illēl.
lines.english: The bus leaves in the afternoon and comes back at night.
How far? An hour.
How often? Every day.
Get on! We leave in a bit.
Today is Eid! Everyone is here.

lines.latin: wlādi, w ilʔaɧfād, w kull il3ēle.
lines.english: My sons, the grandchildren, the whole family.
In God’s name, eat!
May there always be plenty!
It’s raining, and the phone is wet.
Hello? Hello? There’s no sound.

lines.latin: ɧúʈʈu hína, w kamān šwáyye birínn.
lines.english: Put it here, and in a bit it’ll ring.
The phone’s ringing!

lines.arabic: اِبِن عمّي مِن عمّان، وبِنْت خالْتي مِن القُدْس.
lines.latin: íbin 3ámmi min 3ammān, w bint xálti min ilquds.
lines.english: One cousin is from Amman, and another from Jerusalem.
What’s the last name? The same name!
Remember me? I’m your cousin!
What’s new?

lines.arabic: بدّي أروح مكْتب البريد، والسّوْبر مارْكِت.
lines.latin: bíddi arūɧ máktab ilbarīd, w issūbar mārkit.
lines.english: I need the post office and the supermarket.
And where’s my passport?
In my handbag!
And the train station? Where?
Is the suit jacket a bit big?
A bit tight? No!

lines.arabic: أنا ما عملْت جاكيْتّ غلط، وَلا مرّة.
lines.latin: ána ma 3amílt jakētt ɣalaʈ, wala márra.
lines.english: I’ve never once made a jacket wrong.
Put it on, and see!
An apartment building, and I’m at the top.
Do I do the dishes? Make the bed?
Hang out the laundry? How?
But I know fast food!
The results come out on Thursday.
Did I pass? Or fail?

lines.arabic: حظّ بِشِع؟ لا، بدرُس يوْم بعِد يوْم.
lines.latin: ɧaʐʐ bíši3? laʔ, bádrus yōm bá3id yōm.
lines.english: Bad luck? No, I study every other day.

lines.arabic: بسّ أنا مِتْشوِّق زْيادة عن اللُّزوم!
lines.english: But I’m too excited!
I’m a tour guide.
The highway, then the coast.
Do you have a driver’s license?
Pack your suitcase!
Fried eggs? Boiled? Scrambled?
My son is getting married tomorrow!
And the kitchen? It’s mine, for three days!
Close your eyes, and eat!
By day psychology, and by night work.
I have an oral exam and a written exam.
And tuition is expensive.
Sleep? What’s sleep?
It’s stormy, and I’m heading out.
I have a spare tire in the trunk.
A sandstorm? A tornado? I go!
It’s hailing! Look!
This evening: welcome to the show!
First up: folk music!
Then a fairy tale.
Call us!
Do you have a migraine?

lines.latin: xud muɖādd ɧayáwi, w lízig jrūɧ.
lines.english: Take antibiotics, and a Band-Aid.
Are you contagious? No.
And I know everything about you!
I’m the landlord.
The power went out?
Where’s the wrench? In my pocket!
And the mattress? New!
Today is our wedding anniversary, forty years!
We’re in our sixties.
Everyone from town is here!
My darling!
Halloumi? Romy? Cheddar?
And there are mixed nuts.
But before I open, the gym!
The elliptical, and the weights machine.
By day, the hippopotamus.
And by night, music.
And I write everything down.
But nobody knows my name!
Ramallah: the sky is clear.
Gaza: in the mid-twenties.
And Beersheba? Hot!
Have a nice day!
Sit here.
The soup’s in the microwave.
Me? I slept only four hours.
Your hair looks good now!
It’s crowded, and I’m tired.
Let me out here!
Tomorrow, another flight.
Sleep? On the plane!
I live in student housing.
Arabic? I get by.
But my handwriting is awful!
No one understands a word!

lines.arabic: عِنْدي أخو مِن الأبو، وأُخُت مِن الأمّ.
lines.latin: 3índi axu min ilʔabu, w úxut min ilʔumm.
lines.english: I have a half-brother on my father’s side, and a half-sister on my mother’s.
And my stepmother? She’s kind!
And I’m in the middle!
Today we’re all here!
